task: Write a due diligence memo on Rippling

nimble.claim: Parker Conrad is co-founder and CEO of Rippling; previously co-founded Wikinvest/SigFig and Zenefits (CEO, resigned February 2016).
Prasanna Sankar co-founded Rippling in April 2016 and served as CTO (still co-founder/CTO in a March 2019 interview; current status unconfirmed).
Adam Swiecicki is Rippling's Chief Financial Officer (per Yahoo Finance and Crunchbase).
Charles (Matthew) MacInnis is listed as Rippling COO and Bridget Abraham as Chief Compliance Officer on Crunchbase (aggregator data).
In October 2017, Rippling CEO Parker Conrad settled SEC charges (fine paid, no admit/deny) over misleading investors about regulatory compliance at his prior company Zenefits; not a Rippling action.
Rippling Series A: $45M led by Kleiner Perkins (Mamoon Hamid), with Initialized Capital, Threshold Ventures and Y Combinator participating.
Rippling Series B: $145M led by Founders Fund.
Rippling Series C: $250M (October 2021) led by Sequoia Capital Global Equities and Global Growth, with Greenoaks participating; $6.5B valuation per TacticalVC.
Rippling Series D: $250M (May 2022) co-led by Bedrock and Kleiner Perkins, with Y Combinator and Sequoia; valued at $11.25B.
Rippling Series E: $500M (March 2023) led by Greenoaks at $11.25B valuation, closed in about 12 hours during the SVB collapse to cover customer payrolls.

Rippling Series F: $200M new financing plus repurchase of up to $590M of equity from employees, former employees and early investors, at $13.5B valuation (Reuters reported it as Coatue-led, April 2024).

Rippling Series G (May 2025): $450M new financing plus up to $200M employee equity repurchase, at $16.8B valuation; investors include Elad Gil, Sands Capital, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Baillie Gifford and Y Combinator (no lead per Sacra).
Rippling's total funding reached $1.85B with Series G; Rippling said an IPO was not imminent (CNBC).
Rippling sells a unified cloud platform of over two dozen products across HR, IT and Spend (payroll, benefits, SSO/identity, bill pay, corporate cards).

Rippling's business model is per-employee-per-month SaaS subscriptions by module, plus transactional revenue from FX on international payroll, card interchange, instant wage transfers and Employer of Record services.
Rippling claims payroll and workforce management support in 185+ countries on a single platform.
Rippling is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in Ireland (European HQ Dublin), the UK, India (Bengaluru) and Australia (Sydney, first APAC office).
Rippling launched Rippling AI and, in June 2026, Rippling Data Cloud, a business-intelligence product connecting organizational and third-party data.
Rippling had 20,000+ customers as of May 2025 (TechCrunch).
Rippling company-claimed ARR: $175M (2022), $350M (end 2023), $570M (early 2025), $1B+ (April 2026), ~78% YoY growth, with growth accelerating three consecutive quarters into 2026.
Sacra estimates Rippling reached $1B annualized revenue in March 2026, up from $850M at end of 2025, growing 78% YoY (aggregator estimate).
Rippling claims 99.5% PEO customer retention in Fall 2024 renewals; 10+ product lines each exceed $1M ARR, with new products reaching $1M ARR within 5-6 months.
Rippling net revenue retention was approximately 200% as of May 2022 (Contrary Research estimate) vs 110-120% median for enterprise SaaS.
Sigma360 and Rippling announced a partnership in June 2026 for real-time sanctions screening across Rippling's global payments infrastructure.
Named Rippling customers include Walker Advertising, Morning Consult and Four Hands (company claim).

Rippling is in prolonged litigation with competitor Deel (RICO/trade-secret espionage case since March 2025, Deel countersuit); several Deel counterclaims survive, creating management distraction and discovery exposure.
Rippling reportedly faced scrutiny for facilitating payments to contractors in Russia amid sanctions, with possible banking-partner implications (Yahoo Finance profile; unverified against a docket).
Rippling's Glassdoor rating is down 4% over 12 months and only 34% of reviewers approve of the CEO.
Rippling was still unprofitable as of 2024 (Reuters) and relied on primary financing plus employee-equity buybacks ($590M Series F, $200M Series G tender).
The March 2023 SVB collapse froze Rippling's funds and briefly halted customer payrolls, until ~$500M emergency funding was raised; an operational concentration risk event.
Glassdoor: Rippling overall rating 3.6/5 from 1,300+ reviews; 66% would recommend, 75% positive outlook; work-life balance 3.0, culture and values 3.5, career opportunities 3.9.
Glassdoor: Rippling Customer Support employees rate the company 3.0/5 (20 reviews), 22% below the IT-industry average, with support compensation rated 2.8/5.
Glassdoor: Rippling compensation and benefits rated 3.9/5 and stable over 12 months.
Rippling's annual revenue was around $1B as of July 2026 (Wikipedia citing a TechCrunch interview with Parker Conrad; company claim).
Rippling headcount: ~2,800 (2024, Reuters), 5,000 (2025); Latka reports 5,000 as of Nov 2025, up from 3,630 a year earlier (aggregator).
UnifyGTM shows 7,415 Rippling employee profiles in July 2026 (profile-coverage measure, not company-reported).
Rippling held $1 billion in cash for expansion as of 2024 while remaining unprofitable (Reuters via Wikipedia).
Blind posts (unverified) reference Rippling layoffs around August-September 2022; no verified numbers found.
Rippling stated it was hiring across all roles at the May 2025 Series G announcement.
In March 2025 Rippling sued Deel in Ireland alleging corporate espionage; Deel countersued and filed an anti-SLAPP motion in Delaware.

On Feb 25, 2026, Judge Breyer (N.D. Cal.) issued a 49-page ruling letting Rippling's civil RICO and trade secret suit against Deel, its CEO, COO and Board Chair proceed, finding three plausible predicate acts: obstruction of justice, wire fraud, trade secret theft (company claim).

Per Bloomberg (Sept 26, 2026), the federal judge refused to strike a central witness's testimony in the Rippling-Deel case, refused to reopen his ruling letting Rippling's claims proceed, sent Deel's most serious counterclaims to arbitration, and dismissed several Deel false-advertising claims while allowing others to proceed.
In April 2025 the alleged Deel spy admitted to espionage, which Fortune called a major scandal rocking the HR world.

exa.claim: Rippling was founded by Parker Conrad (CEO) and Prasanna Sankar; CNBC dates launch to 2016 and notes Conrad's prior exit from Zenefits.

Rippling leadership as of 2026-10-21: Parker Conrad (co-founder/CEO), Matt MacInnis (President/CPO), Matt Plank (CRO), Adam Swiecicki (CFO), Martin White (General Counsel), Stephanie Ho (SVP Customer Experience), Sunil Raman (SVP Business and Product Operations), Bridget Abraham (Chief Compliance Officer).
Rippling named Albert Strasheim CTO and SVP Engineering (announced 2024-09-06); he was previously VP Engineering at Segment.
Chris Campbell announced on 2025-10-31 he was leaving Rippling after five years as Deputy General Counsel (self-reported departure).
Rippling Series D: $250 million co-led by Bedrock and Kleiner Perkins at an $11.25 billion valuation (company announcement).
Rippling Series E: $500 million led by Greenoaks, raised in response to the March 2023 Silicon Valley Bank failure (company announcement).

Rippling Series F: Reuters reported $200 million primary capital led by Coatue at a $13.5 billion valuation on 2024-04-22, plus a separate tender offer of up to $590 million for employees and early investors (not primary capital).

Rippling Series G: $450 million primary financing announced 2025-05-09 at a $16.8 billion valuation, with investors including Elad Gil, Sands Capital, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Baillie Gifford and Y Combinator; also agreements for up to $200 million of employee/former-employee equity repurchases.
As of CNBC's 2026-05-19 profile, Rippling's latest financing benchmark remains the May 2025 Series G at $16.8 billion valuation; no later valuation found.
TechCrunch reported Rippling's cumulative funding at $1.85 billion as of 2025-05-09 (press-reported).
Rippling offers workforce-management software unifying HR, IT and finance around employee data (payroll, recruiting, device management, expenses) for businesses (company claim).
Rippling pricing is modular, mostly per employee per month; advertised plans start at $8 per employee per month plus a monthly base fee (observed 2026-10-21); actual pricing requires a quote.

Rippling claims to serve businesses from one employee to thousands across multiple countries, with global hiring and payroll offerings in 185+ countries and 50+ currencies (product-specific coverage).
Rippling claims more than 30,000 customers as of 2026-10-21 (comparison page referencing September 2026 information).
TechCrunch reported Rippling had more than 20,000 customers as of 2025-05-09.
Rippling's customer stories name Chess.com, Kleiner Perkins, Dude Wipes, NinjaTech AI, The Channel Company and Clariti as customers.
Y Combinator became a Rippling customer in early 2025; company claims cited by TechCrunch also name Cursor, Clay and Sierra as customers.
Sequoia (the benefits adviser, not Sequoia Capital) has a compensation-and-benefits partnership integrating with Rippling HCM and benefits administration.
Parker Conrad said in April 2026 that Rippling revenue was growing 78% year over year and growth had accelerated for three consecutive quarters (company claim reported by CNBC, unaudited).
CNBC reported Rippling's ARR crossed $1 billion in 2025; no audited statements supplied, and the timing conflicts with Sacra's estimate, requiring reconciliation.
Sacra estimates Rippling reached $1 billion annualized revenue in March 2026, up from $850 million at year-end 2025, with 78% year-over-year growth (third-party estimates).
TechCrunch, citing The Information's sources, reported Rippling had about $570 million annualized revenue around 2025-05-09 (unaudited estimate).
TechCrunch reported Rippling had more than 4,000 employees as of 2025-05-09.
Rippling (People Center, Inc.) sued Deel and executives in March 2025 in N.D. California (case 25-cv-02576-CRB) alleging corporate espionage; these are allegations, not established liability.
A 2026-02-23 court order allowed most of Rippling's claims against Deel, including RICO, to proceed at the pleading stage.

Deel asserted counterclaims against Rippling, Parker Conrad and former employee Keith O'Brien; a 2026-09-25 order partly granted and partly denied dismissal, compelled arbitration, denied a motion to strike, and let some comparative-advertising claims survive; no final resolution.

The 2026-09-25 order discusses contested Russia/sanctions-related statements in the Rippling-Deel dispute; it is civil litigation, not a regulator finding against Rippling, and regulatory exposure is unresolved.
Red flag: Glassdoor shows a declining Rippling employee rating and workload complaints, a trigger to test attrition and support staffing.
Glassdoor (2026-10-21): Rippling rated 3.6/5 across 1,300 reviews, 66% recommend, 80% CEO approval; overall rating declined 4% over the prior twelve months.
Anonymous Rippling employee reviews cite workload, burnout, management and work-life-balance concerns, alongside positive comments on colleagues, learning and product quality.
BBB lists 80 complaints against Rippling over three years and 35 closed in the prior twelve months, covering cancellation, billing, onboarding and support issues (no customer-volume denominator).
CNBC describes the contested Rippling-Deel litigation and reports a criminal investigation into Deel (not Rippling).

firecrawl.claim: Rippling sells an all-in-one workforce-management platform spanning HR, payroll, IT, Finance/Spend, workflows and AI, built on unified workforce data (company claim).

Rippling's product ecosystem includes HRIS, benefits, PEO, HR services, headcount planning, recruiting, performance management, LMS, time and attendance, payroll, IT and finance products, with 650+ integrations advertised (company claim).

Rippling offers EOR, global payroll, global contractor payments and contractor-of-record services, including local-currency payroll and global tax filing, for businesses managing employees and contractors (company claim).
Rippling's site displays named customers including Blank Street Coffee, Chess.com, Barry's, Y Combinator, Kleiner Perkins, Clay and CookUnity (company claim).
Rippling's global page says it is trusted by 25,000+ businesses (company claim).
Reuters reported Rippling served over 20,000 customers in May 2025 and offered more than 20 products across HR, IT and finance management.
Rippling's careers page reports 6,000+ global employees, $35B of payroll processed, 30,000 employee devices managed, 600+ app integrations and 3x year-over-year revenue growth (company claim).
Rippling says 17 Wavemakers were selected from more than 75,000 Rippling admins, and each uses an average of 13 Rippling products (company claim, Nov 2024).
CNBC reported Rippling crossed $1B in annual recurring revenue in 2025, and CEO Parker Conrad said revenue was growing 78% year over year in April 2026 (company-reported figure).
Parker Conrad and Prasanna Sankar founded Rippling in 2016; Conrad is CEO.
Albert Strasheim is Rippling's CTO and SVP of Engineering; previously VP of Engineering at Segment and held senior engineering roles at D2iQ and Cloudflare.
Eisar Lipkovitz is Rippling's Chief Product Officer; previously CIO of JPMorgan's Corporate & Investment Bank, EVP and Head of Rideshare at Lyft, and 15 years at Google.
Matt MacInnis is Rippling's Chief Operating Officer, and Adil Syed is CFO; Syed joined from Snap, where he was Head of Strategy and Operations and helped lead Snap's IPO.

Wan Agus (formerly CTO at Credit Karma) and Gang Wang (formerly CTO at Nuvei, with senior engineering roles at Stripe and Intuit) joined Rippling in December 2025 as SVPs of Engineering (company claim).

Rippling announced a $450M Series G on May 9, 2025 at a $16.8B valuation, plus agreements to repurchase up to $200M of equity from current and former employees; participants included Elad Gil, Sands Capital, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Baillie Gifford and Y Combinator.
CNBC reported Rippling's $450M round had no lead investor, and the $16.8B valuation was up from $13.5B in a round a year earlier.

Fireround records Rippling's total raised at $1.847B across eight rounds: $7M (2017), $45M Series A (2019), $145M Series B (2020), $250M Series C (2021), $250M Series D (2022), $500M (2023), $200M Series F (2024) and $450M Series G (2025).
Rippling's latest publicly evidenced primary valuation is $16.8B, set in the May 2025 Series G.
Reuters reported Rippling was not profitable in May 2025, had well surpassed $100M in ARR and continued choosing growth over profitability.
CEO Parker Conrad told CNBC in May 2025 that Rippling's annual revenue growth was well over 30%; CNBC noted The Information reported ARR above $350M at end of 2023.
Rippling's timeline reports 260 employees onboarded in 2020, versus 6,000+ employees now, indicating substantial headcount expansion (unaudited).
Conrad said Rippling was not planning a near-term IPO and needed to become profitable before going public; CNBC also reported he had avoided layoffs.

Rippling sued Deel in N.D. Cal. in March 2025, alleging a corporate-espionage scheme involving a former Rippling employee, with claims including RICO, trade-secret misappropriation, tortious interference and unfair competition (allegations only, no final merits finding).

A Feb 23, 2026 federal order in People Center, Inc. v. Deel denied the forum-non-conveniens, personal-jurisdiction and service challenges and most dismissal requests, but granted in part dismissal of Rippling's state-law claims; core federal claims continue.

The Rippling v. Deel docket remained active in October 2026: a Sept 25 order granted in part and denied in part a motion to dismiss, granted a motion to compel and denied a motion to strike, followed by a joint discovery letter brief filed Oct 19.

Reuters reported a former Rippling employee admitted in an affidavit made public in an Irish court to spying for Deel under direction of Deel's CEO (reported litigation evidence, not a regulatory adjudication).
The Feb 2026 court order recites Rippling's allegations that the former employee accessed and transmitted confidential information from Rippling's Salesforce, Slack and Google repositories.
Glassdoor shows Rippling at 3.6/5 from 1,300 reviews, with 66% recommending, 80% CEO approval and 75% positive business outlook; senior management and work-life balance each score 3.0/5.
A June 2026 Glassdoor review of Rippling cited low pay relative to workload, poor work-life balance, understaffing, high pressure and high turnover (individual unverified review).

Trustpilot shows Rippling at a 4.5/5 TrustScore from 2,576 reviews; recent reviews are positive on usability and onboarding but note technical issues, slow loading, complex implementation and complicated timesheets.

Red flag: Rippling's reported funding totals conflict, with its careers page saying $1.4B+ raised versus Fireround's $1.847B; needs reconciliation against primary financing documents and tender-offer treatment.
Red flag: Rippling is described as not profitable and not preparing an immediate IPO, making the path to profitability and liquidity a material underwriting question.
